![](/content/exams/anzca/2017/A/11/standard-image31.png){fig-alt="Expiratory flow-volume curves in normal, obstructive and restrictive lungs"}

Normal lungs: 

FVC \~4.5l (65ml/kg)

RV \~1.5l (15-20ml/kg)

PEF \~8l/s

High PEFR due to airways dilation at increased lung volume - resistance limited  

Linear down sloping effort independent expiratory flow line as airways calibre decreases with lung volume 

**Obstructive lung disease:**

TLC and RV ↑ due to gas trapping 

TLC ↑

PEF reduced due to reduced airways calibre in obstructive disease, ↓airway radius → ↑resistance as per  Hagen Poiseuille equation:

R= 8nl/πr4

**Restrictive lung disease:**

TLC reduced due to decreased lung compliance

RV unchanged 

PEF may be same or if reduced but in proportion to ↓FVC, FEV1/FCV ration should be unchanged \>0.7

Effort independent expository line is linear
